name: CoreWeave, Inc. Class A
why: CoreWeaves stronger-than-expected Q3 results and raised outlook, alongside a financing plan centered on customer prepayments rather than new unsecured debt, drove attention and optimism about AI-computing demand. Traders welcomed the update and speculated about short covering, while others argued that heavy debt, capital spending and continuing losses leave financing and profitability risks unresolved.

name: NextNav Inc.
why: NextNavs quarterly results and earnings call are driving attention: traders cite an earnings beat and revenue growth, but are debating the share-price drop despite a reportedly positive call. The broader bull-bear divide remains focused on the pending FCC process for its 900 MHz spectrum, with approval and potential buyers still uncertain.

name: Kura Oncology, Inc.
why: Kuras Q3 results and earnings call are driving discussion, with traders highlighting KOMZIFTIs growing prescriptions and patient starts, alongside an EPS beat. Reactions are broadly favorable to the launch and managements rebuttal of J&Js competing-drug data, though some remain cautious about competition and the stocks weak price action.

name: RUM Group Inc. Class A
why: Rumbles Q3 resultsstrong revenue growth and its first adjusted-EBITDA-profitable quarter, driven in part by Quake AI and Northern Dataare the main focus. Bulls see evidence the AI-infrastructure expansion is gaining traction, while skeptics point to cash needs, potential dilution and delays to some planned capacity, questioning whether the results will translate into lasting value.

name: Applied Materials, Inc.
why: AMATs upcoming earnings and guidance are a key focus, with traders looking for evidence that AI-driven chipmaking investment is sustaining equipment orders. Bulls view the sector selloff as a buying opportunity, while bears question whether capex is being pulled forward and point to financing and export-policy risks.

name: USA Rare Earth, Inc. Class A
Capricor Therapeutics, Inc.
why: Capricors upcoming FDA decision on deramiocel for Duchenne muscular dystrophy is the dominant focus, with the company saying its application is in final review and reaffirming confidence after its earnings call. Traders are divided between optimism over the upper-limb trial data and launch preparations, and concern that the FDA could still reject the application given the prior advisory committees negative view of the cardiac data.

name: NVIDIA Corporation
why: Nvidia is drawing attention over the allegations and investigation involving Jensen Huang, with traders debating whether the China-related concerns could bring leadership or regulatory risksor are personal-news noise that does not change the business. Bairds downgrade and concerns about AI-spending visibility add pressure, while CoreWeaves results have encouraged dip-buying and a rebound that some traders doubt will last.

name: BlackBerry Limited
why: BlackBerrys expanding QNX partnerships are driving attention, particularly its integration into Valeos smart-camera platform, which has design wins with multiple automakers in China. Bulls view the wins as evidence of future growth in automotive software, while skeptics want to see design wins and the reported backlog convert into revenue.

name: Rigetti Computing, Inc.
why: Rigettis Q3 results missed expectations and its revenue outlook disappointed, prompting concern that commercial demand is lagging its quantum-computing ambitions. Traders are divided: bears question the valuation and long path to meaningful revenue, while bulls point to technical progress, cash reserves and government support as reasons to stay focused on the long term.

name: AAON, Inc.
why: AAON raised its full-year growth forecast to 72-75%, up from 55-60%, following strong Q3 earnings with 84% net sales growth and 207% growth in its AI-focused BASX segment

name: Zeta Global Holdings Corp. Class A
why: Zeta Global topped Q3 2026 earnings and revenue estimates, beating consensus estimates by 35.71% on EPS and exceeding revenue expectations by 4.72%
ref: Zeta Global Holdings reported Q3 2026 earnings of $0.38 per share, beating consensus estimates by 35.71%, with revenues of $492.66 million exceeding expectations by 4.72%.

name: Amprius Technologies Inc
why: Amprius Technologies reported Q3 earnings with a revenue beat of $39.15 million (82.8% year-over-year growth) but missed EPS estimates with a loss of $0.02 per share versus consensus estimate of $0.01 loss

name: Hims & Hers Health, Inc. Class A
why: Q3 2026 earnings miss with EPS of $0.03 versus $0.07 consensus estimate and revenues of $890.37 million missing estimates
ref: Hims & Hers reported Q3 2026 earnings of $0.03 per share, missing the consensus estimate of $0.07 per share, representing a -57.14% earnings surprise. Revenues of $890.37 million also missed estimates by 0.34%.

name: Netlist, Inc.
why: Netlists Q3 results and outlook have put its Samsung and Micron licensing agreements, improved profitability, and expected business growth in focus. Traders are broadly optimistic and read the CEOs comments as a hint of a possible SK Hynix licensing deal, though that agreement remains unconfirmed; some also question the earnings-estimate miss and lower product sales.

name: Stellar Lumens
why: Traders are debating Stellars planned role in DTCC tokenization and broader real-world-asset adoption, with some viewing institutional integrations as a long-term positive. Others point to XLMs persistent weakness and question whether partnerships and network activity will translate into meaningful token demand.

name: Zcash
why: Zcash is drawing attention for a sharp, volatile pullback after a strong rally, with traders debating whether it reflects profit-taking and an unwind or broader crypto-market weakness. Bearish posts call the move a rug pull and expect further losses, while bullish traders view the dip as a buying opportunity and continue accumulating.
